title: New list/collection endpoints must use the Acme {items,total} envelope with limit/offset validation, not a bare array

reviews.notes: Verified against code/tests (ev:ev-muzm4t8z-01b97604): title general, AG-7 quoted verbatim, notApplicableWhen sensible.

symptoms: collection endpoint response is not {"items": [...], "total": n}
invalid limit should be 422 validation_failed fields ["limit"]
rootCause: Implementation followed the ticket and returned a bare array. Verbatim, guideline AG-7: "collection endpoints return {\"items\": [...], \"total\": <number of matching records>}. They accept ?limit (default 50, max 100; invalid values are rejected with 422 validation_failed, fields: [\"limit\"]) and ?offset (default 0). Bare JSON arrays are allowed only on legacy endpoints that already return them." Source: QA feedback, guideline AG-7. The rule lives in QA feedback, not the ticket or vendor/acme-kit README, so it was never consulted up front.

failedAttempts.approach: Return the filtered, sorted array directly (what the ticket described)
failedAttempts.whyFailed: Bare arrays are allowed only for legacy endpoints that already return them; GET /api/notes is new.

fix: Return {items: page, total: matching.length} where total counts every record matching the filter (e.g. ?tag) before limit/offset. Parse limit/offset as strict base-10 digit strings (/^\d+$/): limit 1..100 default 50 (0, >100, empty, decimal, negative, non-numeric rejected), offset >= 0 default 0 (invalid rejected, our decision, documented in README). Throw HttpError(422,"validation_failed",...,{fields}) listing "limit" and/or "offset". Update existing tests that asserted bare arrays; leave legacy endpoints (GET /api/tags) unchanged. Up front: read vendor/acme-kit README and look at existing conventions before designing a new endpoint.
appliesWhen: Adding a new list/collection endpoint in an Acme service
Adding pagination (limit/offset) or a total count to an endpoint
Writing tests for a GET that returns many records
notApplicableWhen: Legacy endpoints that already return bare arrays, e.g. GET /api/tags (mobile parses it); keep their format

title: Every new create/update/delete endpoint must write exactly one audit_log row (actor, action, entity, entity_id, at) in the same synchronous step

reviews.notes: Verified against code/tests (ev:ev-muzm4t8z-01b97604): title general, SEC-12 quoted verbatim, notApplicableWhen sensible.

symptoms: audit_log table is empty after a write request
rootCause: Implementation covered only the functional ticket. Verbatim, rule SEC-12: "every request that creates, changes or deletes data writes exactly one row to the service's audit_log table: actor (the X-Acme-Actor request header, or \"anonymous\" if absent), action (create, update or delete), entity (the table name), entity_id (the affected row id) and at (ISO-8601 timestamp). Rejected requests write nothing." Source: QA feedback, rule SEC-12. The rule was not in the ticket; the pre-existing audit_log table in fixtures/db.json was the up-front clue.

failedAttempts.approach: Implement only the ticket behaviour (insert the note)
Considered writing the audit row in a separate awaited step
failedAttempts.whyFailed: An await between data change and audit insert allows a note without its row (crash/interleaving); do both synchronously.

fix: Add a reusable helper audited(db, req, {action, entity}, write) that runs the synchronous write, then inserts the audit_log row with actor = trimmed X-Acme-Actor or "anonymous" (absent, empty or whitespace), entity_id = result.id, at = new Date().toISOString(). No await between the two. Call it only after validation so rejected requests (422/400/413/415) write nothing. Tests: one row with exact fields, anonymous variants, no rows for rejected requests and reads. Here it lives at src/notes/audit.js (task scope); move to src/audit.js to share across modules.
appliesWhen: Adding a new create, update or delete endpoint in an Acme service
Adding any code path that inserts, updates or removes rows
Reviewing a feature for audit/security rules not in the ticket
notApplicableWhen: Requests rejected by validation (they must write nothing)
Writes to the audit_log table itself

verificationEvidence.label: repro: AG-7 envelope/pagination and SEC-12 audit missing
fix verified: AG-7 envelope/pagination and SEC-12 audit

title: A POST endpoint that moves money (refund, payout, credit, charge) must honour the Idempotency-Key header, or retries duplicate the money movement

reviews.notes: Corrected: table moved to src/db.js (fixtures outside task ownership); evidence refs updated

symptoms: POST /api/customers/2/credits twice with Idempotency-Key console-7f3a9c returned 201 id 6 then 201 id 7 (same amount 20.00 and reason)
duplicate money movement on retry or double click; refund, payout, credit or charge created twice
repeated request with the same key creates a new row instead of replaying the original status and body
rootCause: The handler never read the Idempotency-Key header and kept no record of processed keys, so every POST executed addCredit. Organisational rule PAY-3, source 'QA feedback, rule PAY-3', verbatim: "a POST endpoint that moves money (refunds, payouts, credits, charges) honours the Idempotency-Key request header. A repeated request with the same key returns the original status and body, and creates nothing new. A request without the header behaves normally."

failedAttempts.approach: Searched memory for prior lessons on idempotency, duplicate POSTs and repeated requests
failedAttempts.whyFailed: No matching memory records existed, so the design came from the PAY-3 text and the acme-kit conventions.

failedAttempts.approach: Considered de-duplicating by comparing amount and reason against recent credits
failedAttempts.whyFailed: Rejected before implementing: legitimate identical credits would be blocked and keyless requests must keep behaving normally. Only the client-supplied key identifies a retry.

fix: Add an idempotency_keys table (customer_id, endpoint, idem_key, request_hash, status, response, created_at). Scope the key per customer and endpoint. Read the header after the 404 check, so unknown customers store nothing. A present but empty or over-255-char key is 422 naming Idempotency-Key. After body validation, run lookup, addCredit and key recording in one synchronous step with no await in between (withIdempotency in repository.js), so concurrent duplicates create exactly one credit. A hit with the same normalized request (cents and trimmed reason) replays the stored status and body verbatim. A hit with a different request is 422 validation_failed with fields ['Idempotency-Key']. No header leaves the old path untouched. Apply the same wrapper to every future refund, payout or charge POST.
appliesWhen: adding or changing a POST endpoint that moves money: refund, payout, credit, charge, top-up, transfer
a client may retry or double-submit (support console, checkout, webhook-driven calls)
QA or finance reports duplicate credits, double refunds or double charges
task text mentions Idempotency-Key, idempotent, replay or retry-safe
notApplicableWhen: POST endpoints that do not move money (e.g. notes, preferences, search)
PUT or DELETE that are naturally idempotent by resource id
bugs where a keyless request is wrongly deduplicated; the rule says a request without the header behaves normally

title: CSV exports for accounting must quote every text field per Acme spec ACC-2, not minimal RFC 4180 quoting

reviews.notes: Checked against csv.js and csv.test.js and approved gate phase:rework-1 (npm test ev-muzlhelz-013bbd98 passes). Always-quote fix, unquoted amounts, CRLF and raw-text assertion are all present; the failed-attempt note (round-trip parser cannot detect missing quotes) is accurate. Scope limits are appropriate.

symptoms: header row is not quoted, /api/reports/sales.csv?month=2026-09 line 1: order_number,customer,placed_on,total
CSV for accounting import: text fields not wrapped in double quotes
CSV valid per RFC 4180 but fails organisational format spec
rootCause: Implementation assumed RFC 4180 minimal quoting; the organisational rule is stricter. Verbatim, Acme accounting interface spec ACC-2: "CSV files for accounting use CRLF (\r\n) line endings, start with a header row, wrap every text field in double quotes (doubling embedded quotes), and write amounts as plain decimals with two digits." Source: QA feedback, Acme accounting interface spec ACC-2.

failedAttempts.approach: Original design: quote only when needed (RFC 4180) and test via a round-trip parser
failedAttempts.whyFailed: A parser that accepts both quoted and unquoted fields cannot detect missing quotes; tests passed while the spec was violated.

sources.title: QA feedback, Acme accounting interface spec ACC-2

fix: Make the field escaper always wrap in double quotes (doubling embedded quotes, after formula neutralisation) and route header names, dates, TOTAL label and empty text fields through it; leave amounts as unquoted two-decimal numbers; keep CRLF. Assert raw output text in tests, not only parsed rows.
appliesWhen: CSV exports for accounting in Acme services
Writing or testing a CSV serializer that must follow an organisational format spec stricter than RFC 4180
notApplicableWhen: Other consumers that have their own CSV spec

verificationEvidence.label: repro: AC8 header/text fields not quoted
